parameters.x-ms-description-for-model: SharePoint site URL or 'me' for personal OneDrive. Must exactly match the value from policy or user context -- do not guess or invent URLs. Examples of real formats: 'me', 'https://contoso.sharepoint.com/sites/Operations', '/sites/insurance'.

parameters.name: drive

parameters.description: Select an Excel file through File Browse.
parameters.x-ms-description-for-model: Excel filename including .xlsx extension (e.g. 'CapacityPlanning.xlsx', 'QuoteLog.xlsx'). May include a path prefix. Use exactly the value from policy or user context.

parameters.name: table
parameters.description: Excel table.

post.x-ms-description-for-model:
Creates a new named table in an Excel file from a specified cell range and optional column definitions.
- Use this only when the table does not already exist. If the table exists, use add_row_into_table to add data to it.
- To discover existing tables, use get_tables.
- table_range defines the initial extent. Match the column count to the number of columns_names provided.
- Always provide columns_names to define the schema explicitly.

parameters.description: Select a table from the drop-down.

parameters.name: idColumn
parameters.description: Provide the key column name.
parameters.x-ms-description-for-model: Optional. Name of the key column to add or reposition (e.g. 'LookupKey', 'ID'). Defaults to 'ID' if not provided. This column can then be used as key_column in get_row, update_row, and delete_row.

post.x-ms-description-for-model:
Adds or repositions a key column in an existing Excel table. If the column already exists, it is moved to the rightmost position. If it does not exist, a new empty column is appended.
- Use this to establish a key column for row lookups via get_row, update_row, and delete_row.
- Not for adding data rows (use add_row_into_table) or creating tables (use create_table).
- Rarely needed: most tables already have a usable key column. Only use when instructed or when no existing column can serve as a unique identifier.

get.x-ms-description-for-model: Use tool to list, read and filter rows in a table inside an Excel file. Example user intent: Read and list the Budget table in the Finance.xlsx file.

parameters.name: source
parameters.description:
Select from the drop-down or specify one of the following:
            - "me"
            - "SharePoint Site URL"
            - "users/someone's UPN"
            - "groups/group Id"
            - "sites/SharePoint Site URL:/teams/team name:" (the colons are required)
parameters.x-ms-description-for-model: Set this to the storage location identifier for the workbook. Use me for the current user's OneDrive, the full SharePoint site URL for a site, users/{UPN} for another user's OneDrive, groups/{GroupId} for a Microsoft 365 group, or sites/{SiteURL}:/teams/{TeamName}: for a Team path (colons are required). Examples: me; https://contoso.sharepoint.com/sites/Marketing; users/alice@contoso.com; groups/12345678-aaaa-bbbb-cccc-123456789000

parameters.name: drive
parameters.description: Select a document library from the drop-down.
parameters.x-ms-description-for-model: Set to the document library name that contains the workbook. This is usually "OneDrive" if location parameter is "me". Example: OneDrive, Documents.

parameters.name: file
parameters.description: Select an Excel file through File Browse.
parameters.x-ms-description-for-model: Set to the workbook path starting with a forward slash, including subfolders and the .xlsx extension. Example: /Reports/2025/Financials.xlsx.

parameters.name: table
parameters.description: Select a table from the drop-down.
parameters.x-ms-description-for-model: Set to the Excel table name inside the workbook, not the sheet name. Example: SalesTable.

parameters.name: $filter
parameters.description: An ODATA filter query to restrict the entries returned.
parameters.x-ms-description-for-model: Set to a single OData $filter expression to narrow rows, using one condition with eq or ne or functions contains, startswith, endswith, and string values in single quotes. Example: City eq 'Seattle'.

parameters.name: $orderby
parameters.description: An ODATA orderBy query for specifying the order of entries.
parameters.x-ms-description-for-model: Use to sort the results by a single column. Set by using the column header name, followed by asc or desc. Only one column is allowed. Examples: Date desc, Price asc, Name asc.

parameters.name: $top
parameters.description: Total number of entries to retrieve (default = all).
parameters.x-ms-description-for-model: Set this to a positive integer to limit the number of rows returned. For example, map phrases like "top 5" to 5 or "first 10" to 10.

parameters.name: $skip
parameters.description: The number of entries to skip (default = 0).
parameters.x-ms-description-for-model: Set this to a nonnegative integer (e.g. 5) to skip the first N rows, for example when doing pagination or if the user asks for something "skip the first 5 rows".

parameters.name: $select
parameters.description: Comma-separated list of columns to retrieve (first 500 by default).
parameters.x-ms-description-for-model: Set to a comma separated list of column names to return when only specific columns are needed. Example: Name,Email,Phone.

parameters.name: idColumn
parameters.description: Select a column from the drop-down.

parameters.name: dateTimeFormat
parameters.description: DateTime Format.
parameters.x-ms-description-for-model: Set to how date values are represented, using only either ISO 8601 or Serial Number. Prefer ISO 8601 unless the user states otherwise.

get.x-ms-description-for-model: Use this tool to find and retrieve a single row from an Excel table by key column lookup. Examples: 'Find the record for ID 123', 'Get details for Project Alpha', 'Look up Alice's status'.

parameters.name: source
parameters.description:
Select from the drop-down or specify one of the following:
            - "me"
            - "SharePoint Site URL"
            - "users/someone's UPN"
            - "groups/group Id"
            - "sites/SharePoint Site URL:/teams/team name:" (the colons are required)
parameters.x-ms-description-for-model: Set this to the storage location identifier. Use me for current user's OneDrive, SharePoint site URL, users/{UPN} for another user's OneDrive, groups/{GroupId} for a group, or sites/{URL}:/teams/{name}: for Teams. Do not invent URLs.

parameters.name: drive
parameters.description: Select a document library from the drop-down.
parameters.x-ms-description-for-model: Set to the document library containing the workbook. Usually OneDrive if location is me, or Documents/Shared Documents for SharePoint.

parameters.name: file
parameters.description: Select an Excel file through File Browse.
parameters.x-ms-description-for-model: Set to the workbook path you will query starting with /, including subfolders and .xlsx extension. Examples: /Book1.xlsx, /Reports/2025/Financials.xlsx.

parameters.name: table
parameters.description: Select a table from the drop-down.
parameters.x-ms-description-for-model: Set to the Excel table name you will retrieve row from (not sheet name). Examples: Table1, SalesTable.

parameters.x-ms-description-for-model: Set to the column in the table that acts as the lookup key for this action. Examples: EmployeeID, SKU, EmailAddress.

parameters.x-ms-description-for-model: Set to either ISO 8601 or Serial Number based on how date and time values should be returned. Default to ISO 8601 if not specified.

delete.description: Delete a row using a key column.

parameters.name: source
parameters.description:
Select from the drop-down or specify one of the following:
            - "me"
            - "SharePoint Site URL"
            - "users/someone's UPN"
            - "groups/group Id"
            - "sites/SharePoint Site URL:/teams/team name:" (the colons are required)
parameters.x-ms-description-for-model: SharePoint site URL or 'me' for personal OneDrive. Must exactly match the value from policy or user context -- do not guess or invent URLs.

parameters.name: drive
parameters.description: Select a document library from the drop-down.
parameters.x-ms-description-for-model: Name of the document library (e.g. 'Documents', 'Shared Documents'). Must exactly match the value from policy or user context.

parameters.name: file
parameters.description: Select an Excel file through File Browse.
parameters.x-ms-description-for-model: Excel filename including .xlsx extension (e.g. 'Agent_Risk_Log.xlsx'). May include a path prefix. Use exactly the value from policy or user context.

parameters.name: table
parameters.description: Select a table from the drop-down.
parameters.x-ms-description-for-model: Exact table name as defined in the workbook (case-sensitive, e.g. 'Risks', 'TrainingRecords'). Use the value from policy, user context, or get_tables output.

parameters.name: idColumn
parameters.description: Select a column from the drop-down.
parameters.x-ms-description-for-model: Name of the column that uniquely identifies the row to delete (case-sensitive). Common examples: 'risk_id', 'EmployeeID', 'ProjectKey'. Use the column name exactly as it appears in the table schema.

parameters.name: id
parameters.description: Enter the key value.
parameters.x-ms-description-for-model: The value to match in key_column to locate the row to delete. Always pass as a string, even for numeric IDs (e.g. 'EMP-10042', 'RISK-001').

delete.x-ms-description-for-model:
Deletes a single row from an Excel table, identified by matching a key column to a specific value. This permanently removes the row.
- To modify column values without removing the row, use update_row instead.
- Uses key_column and key_value to find the row -- the same lookup mechanism as get_row and update_row.
- All identifier parameters (location, document_library, file, table) are case-sensitive and must match exactly.

patch.description: Update a row using a key column. The input value will overwrite the specified cells and columns left blank will not be updated. In order to append (instead of overwrite) a value, use the "Get a row" action to retrieve the content first.

parameters.name: source
parameters.description:

parameters.name: drive

parameters.name: file
parameters.description: Select an Excel file through File Browse.
parameters.x-ms-description-for-model: Excel filename including .xlsx extension (e.g. 'Agent_Risk_Log.xlsx', 'QuoteLog.xlsx'). May include a path prefix. Use exactly the value from policy or user context.

parameters.name: table
parameters.description: Select a table from the drop-down.
parameters.x-ms-description-for-model: Exact table name as defined in the workbook (case-sensitive, e.g. 'Risks', 'TrainingRecords'). Use the value from policy, user context, or get_tables output.

parameters.name: idColumn
parameters.description: Select a column from the drop-down.
parameters.x-ms-description-for-model: Name of the column that uniquely identifies the row to update (case-sensitive). Common examples: 'risk_id', 'EmployeeID', 'ProjectKey', 'SKU_ID'. Use the column name exactly as it appears in the table schema.

parameters.name: id
parameters.description: Enter the key value.
parameters.x-ms-description-for-model: The value to match in key_column to locate the target row. Always pass as a string, even for numeric IDs (e.g. 'EMP-10042', 'RISK-001', 'PHX').

parameters.name: item
parameters.description: Provide the item properties.
parameters.x-ms-description-for-model: REQUIRED. A JSON object of column-value pairs to update on the matched row. Keys must be exact column names (case-sensitive). Only include columns you want to change -- unmentioned columns keep their current values. Example: {"status": "mitigated", "description": "Updated risk assessment"}. WARNING: this parameter is named 'item_properties', NOT 'row'. The 'row' parameter belongs to add_row_into_table.

parameters.name: mode
parameters.description: Mode of the operation.

parameters.name: dateTimeFormat
parameters.description: DateTime Format.
parameters.x-ms-description-for-model: Optional. Format string for date/time values in item_properties. Uses UPPERCASE tokens: YYYY, MM, DD, HH, mm, ss. Common values: 'YYYY-MM-DD', 'YYYY-MM-DDTHH:mm:ssZ'. WARNING: do NOT use lowercase 'yyyy-MM-dd' -- only uppercase tokens are accepted. If omitted, date strings are stored as-is.

patch.x-ms-description-for-model:
Updates an existing row in an Excel table, identified by a key column and value. The columns to update MUST be passed in the required 'item_properties' parameter (not 'row').
- To add a new row, use add_row_into_table instead (it takes a 'row' parameter).
- Common mistake: using 'row' instead of 'item_properties', or omitting 'item_properties' entirely.
- Only include the columns you want to change -- unmentioned columns keep their current values.
- The key_column and key_value identify which row to update. Both are case-sensitive.

TableName.x-ms-description-for-model: Optional. Desired name for the new table (e.g. 'Cases', 'UsageSummary', 'FacilityMaturities'). If omitted, an auto-generated name like 'Table1' is used.

Range.description: Enter the table address using A1 notation.
Range.x-ms-description-for-model: Cell range for the table in A1 notation. The range should match the intended table dimensions. Use header-only ranges like 'A1:F1' when rows will be added later via add_row_into_table, or include data rows like 'A1:E3' when the data already exists in the sheet. Can include a sheet prefix like 'Sheet1!A1:D1'. The number of columns should match the number of column names.

ColumnsNames.description: Enter the columns names separated by ';' or ','.
ColumnsNames.x-ms-description-for-model: Optional. Comma-separated column names for the table schema (e.g. 'Bid_ID,Item_Description,Quantity,Unit_Price,Currency,Total_Cost'). Semicolons also accepted as separators but commas are standard. If omitted, the table is created without a predefined column schema.

source.name: source
source.description:
Select from the drop-down or specify one of the following:
              - "me"
              - "SharePoint Site URL"
              - "users/someone's UPN"
              - "groups/group Id"
              - "sites/SharePoint Site URL:/teams/team name:" (colons are required).
source.x-ms-description-for-model: Set this to the storage location identifier for the workbook. Use me for the current user's OneDrive, the full SharePoint site URL for a site, users/{UPN} for another user's OneDrive, groups/{GroupId} for a Microsoft 365 group, or sites/{SiteURL}:/teams/{TeamName}: for a Team path (colons are required). Examples: me; https://zava.sharepoint.com/sites/Sales

drive.name: drive
drive.description: Select a document library from the drop-down.
drive.x-ms-description-for-model: Set to the document library name that contains the Excel workbook. For OneDrive based files often OneDrive; for SharePoint often Documents or another library like Shared Documents.

file.name: file
file.description: Select an Excel file through File Browse.
file.x-ms-description-for-model: Set to the Excel workbook path in the selected library, starting with a forward slash, including subfolders and the .xlsx extension. Example: /Reports/2025/Financials.xlsx.

table.name: table
table.description: Select a table from the drop-down.
table.x-ms-description-for-model: Set to the exact name of the Table object inside the Excel file.This is usually different from the Sheet name. Examples: "Table1"; "SalesTable"; "InventoryData".

fetchSensitivityLabelMetadata.description: A boolean whether to fetch sensitivity label Metadata for associated LabelId.
